Subject: Initial redline: liability scope where confidentiality or trade secrets are implicated

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the thoughtful review. Attached is a narrow redline to Section 7 of the MSA that addresses your team’s ask around removing the liability cap for confidentiality/trade secret events.

Quick context on Redwood’s posture: we understand and accept that certain confidentiality incidents (particularly involving confirmed trade-secret exfiltration or irreparable harm) may justify equitable relief (injunctive relief) and, in narrow cases, damages outside the general cap. At the same time, for commercial predictability, Redwood needs objective triggers and process guardrails (forensics, notice, scope) before uncapping.

Please see the attached: MSA_redline_section_7_unlimited_damages_clause.docx (redline) and a short Forensics_Retention_SOW.pdf that outlines steps and indicative costs. Asha — could you confirm whether Crimson would accept the following high-level working points?

1) Uncapped remedies (including injunctive relief and monetary damages not subject to the general liability cap) are limited to claims that: (a) relate to willful misappropriation of trade secrets by Redwood personnel or contractors, or (b) relate to unauthorized exfiltration of Customer trade secrets as verified by an independent forensic report.
2) Redwood and Customer will follow a defined forensics playbook within 72 hours of notice: preservation hold, agreed vendor/forensic scope, evidence collection, and joint triage. Costs for an independent forensic vendor to be borne by the losing party, but Redwood will advance reasonable costs on a limited basis to avoid preservation delays.
3) Customer must provide timely notice (no later than 60 days after discovery) and reasonable cooperation for the forensics.
4) Remedies remain subject to final adjudication; Redwood will not accept an uncapped liability where Customer fails to meet the notice/evidence requirements.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the redline. Proposed times Monday morning PT.

Best,
Sean

Sean —

Thanks for the redline and the SOW. High level response from legal: Crimson is open to preserving injunctive relief and equitable remedies without displacing the commercial cap, but we need clarity on two items before proceeding: (i) a narrower trigger definition for the uncapped damages bucket (we cannot broadly accept unlimited monetary exposure), and (ii) an acceptable forensics & evidence protocol — specifically who appoints the vendor, timing commitments, and confidentiality of the forensics report.

Two concrete asks from our side:
- Replace “willful misappropriation” with a trigger that includes (A) adjudicated finding of trade-secret misappropriation OR (B) where an independent forensic report (mutually agreed vendor) confirms exfiltration of trade-secret artifacts attributable to Redwood systems/personnel.
- Include a dispute path when parties disagree on the forensics findings (e.g., binding expert determination or expedited arbitration for the limited question of causation).

Can your legal team accept appointing a mutually agreed forensic vendor and an expedited expert-adjudication mechanism limited in scope to causation and trade-secret identity? If so we can move forward to exchange a redline.

—asha

Sean —

This looks reasonable; our legal position below (copy this into the reply):

1) Objective trigger: we will accept an uncapped damages carve-out only where either: (a) there is a final judicial or arbitral determination of willful misappropriation of trade secrets by Redwood (not mere allegation), OR (b) a mutually agreed independent forensic vendor issues a written report within the forensic scope confirming unauthorized exfiltration of artifacts that are reasonably contemporaneous with the claimed incident and attributable to Redwood systems or accounts.
2) Forensics protocol: both parties will agree on a vendor within 5 business days from written notice; evidence preservation steps required within 72 hours; vendor report delivered within 30 calendar days unless extended for good cause. Parties will exchange redacted copies of reports and maintain confidentiality per the MSA.
3) Dispute resolution for causation: agree to an expedited single-expert determination limited to (i) whether the unlabeled artifacts are trade secrets as defined in the MSA and (ii) whether the forensic evidence links exfiltration to Redwood with a preponderance standard. The expert’s determination on those discrete questions will be binding for the purpose of triggering the uncapped remedy but will not decide quantum of damages beyond that scope. If either party declines the expert mechanism, we revert to expedited arbitration limited to causation only.
4) Cost mechanics: the party that does not prevail on causation pays the expert/vendor fees; however, Redwood will advance up to $20k to stand up the engagement to avoid preservation delay (recoverable if Redwood is not the prevailing party).

I also propose we add a notice/limitation guard: if Customer fails to provide the 72-hour preservation or 60-day notice, the uncapped remedy is not available. That protects us from stale claims.

Marcus — please add anything re: evidence retention windows or tech constraints.

If that’s agreeable I’m comfortable we send the counter to Asha with the attached redline and the SOW. We should flag the single-expert binding language as narrowly drawn — that’s our concession in exchange for a clear, fast path.

Laura

Asha —

Thanks for the quick feedback. Please find attached a narrowly tailored counterproposal and a short forensics SOW we use with customers. High-level summary of the counter (copied from internal counsel):

• Triggers for uncapped remedies: (i) final judicial/arbitral finding of willful misappropriation by Redwood, or (ii) mutually agreed independent forensic report confirming unauthorized exfiltration of Customer trade-secret artifacts attributable to Redwood systems/accounts.
• Forensics timelines: 72-hour preservation requirement; vendor agreed within 5 business days; vendor report target 30 days.
• Dispute path: single independent expert (mutually selected) to decide (A) whether the artifacts are trade secrets under MSA definition and (B) whether exfiltration is attributable to Redwood. The expert’s determinations on these points will be binding only to trigger the uncapped remedy; quantum remains subject to the parties’ normal dispute resolution. If a party refuses the expert, we revert to expedited arbitration for causation only.
• Cost mechanics: losing party pays vendor/expert fees; Redwood will advance up to $20,000 to stand up the investigation if needed to avoid preservation delays (recoverable if Redwood does not prevail).
• Notice requirement: Customer must provide written notice within 60 days of discovery of the incident and follow the preservation steps; failure to do so forfeits the uncapped remedy.

We believe this balances Crimson’s need for protection with Redwood’s need for objective triggers and predictable process. Please review the attached redline and SOW and let us know if Crimson can accept the mutual vendor + limited expert mechanism. Happy to set a 30-minute call Monday 9:00–9:30am PT.
